top.title: Missouri Basketball Rolls to Another Dominant Victory Behind Big Performances From Tiller and Crowe
top.description: Photo by: Denny Medley Tigers Set the Tone Early Missouri basketball continued its impressive run Friday afternoon, defeating Arkansas-Pine Bluff 97-61 at Mizzou Arena to earn its sixth consecutive victory. The Tigers entered the matchup looking to finish November on a high note before beginning a much more challenging stretch of their schedule. They accomplished that goal in convincing fashion, controlling the game from the opening minutes and showing their ability to dominate inside. Missouri wasted little time establishing its advantage. The Tigers opened the contest with an 11-0 run and eventually stretched their lead to 16-2 in less than five minutes. Arkansas-Pine Bluff struggled to find an answer for Missouri’s size and offensive pressure. The Golden Lions managed to settle down somewhat as the first half continued, but they never seriously threatened the Tigers’ advantage. Missouri continued attacking the basket, finding opportunities around the rim and creating quality looks through effective ball movement. Bryson Tiller was especially impressive during the opening half, scoring 14 points while making all four of his field-goal attempts. His production helped Missouri take a comfortable 51-28 advantage into halftime. Tiller Leads the Scoring Attack Tiller continued his strong performance throughout the afternoon, finishing with a team high 22 points, six rebounds, two assists and four blocked shots. The forward was difficult for Arkansas-Pine Bluff to contain, consistently using his size and athleticism to create scoring opportunities around the basket. His ability to contribute defensively also made a major difference. Jason Crowe Jr. delivered another impressive performance for the Tigers, finishing with 21 points. The freshman continued showing why he has become such an important part of Missouri’s offense, providing another reliable scoring option alongside Tiller. Mark Mitchell also made an important contribution in his return to the starting lineup. After missing time following a concussion, Mitchell finished with 14 points, three rebounds and three assists. Toni Bryant added 14 points, eight rebounds and four assists, giving Missouri another productive performance from its frontcourt. Missouri’s Defense Makes a Statement While the offense received plenty of attention, Missouri’s defensive performance was arguably just as impressive. The Tigers recorded 13 blocked shots, with Bryant accounting for a career high seven. Tiller added four blocks, helping Missouri make life extremely difficult for Arkansas-Pine Bluff around the basket. Missouri also forced 18 turnovers and recorded 12 steals. The defensive pressure prevented the Golden Lions from developing any consistent offensive rhythm. The Tigers finished shooting 57.6% from the field and scored 50 points in the paint. top.title: Manhunt launched for killers of NSCDC officer in Benue
top.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Chairman of Agatu Local Government Area of Benue State, Mr Melvin Ejeh, has vowed to ensure the arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the killing of an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Inspector Anyebe Anya. Anya was reportedly killed by armed men who attacked him at his duty post at a checkpoint in Agatu a few days ago. The assailants were also said to have carted away his service rifle after the attack. Ejeh gave the assurance when he visited the deceased officer’s family in Otukpo to commiserate with them, describing Anya as a hardworking, honest and dedicated officer. He vowed that those behind the killing would not escape justice, assuring the bereaved family that efforts were already underway to track down and apprehend the perpetrators. “Those that killed him will not go unpunished. We will get all of them. I knew him personally. He was a very hardworking, honest man who was committed to his work. “The whole community is mourning his death. The people of Agatu are shocked and grieving over his death. “We console his family. He was a committed officer. I can assure you that we will get those involved and they will be brought to justice. There is a hunt for them already. “The entire Agatu people will not rest until he gets justice, that I can assure his family,” the chairman said. Efforts to reach the Public Relations Officer of the Benue State NSCDC Command, SC Michael Ejelikwu, for comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. top.title: Recap: Wake Forest’s Comeback Effort Falls Short in 85-88 Loss to #24 Memphis
top.description: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 05: Kevair Kennedy #55 of the Wake Forest Demon Deacons looks on during the second half of the game against the Vanderbilt Commodores at Memorial Gym on November 05, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the final game of the Battle 4 Atlantis, the Deacs dropped their 2nd game of the season to the Memphis Tigers by a score of 85-88. Unbelievable fight falls just short. pic.twitter.com/MAGB94YP9e — Wake Forest Men's Basketball (@WakeMBB) November 27, 2026 The game started off fine for the Deacs, but after Kevair Kennedy picked up his 2nd foul just 6 minutes into the game, things fell apart rapidly. When Kennedy exited the game, the Deacs held a 13-8 lead with 14 minutes remaining in the half—Wake scored 13 points total in those final 14 minutes. Without Kennedy, the Deacs just don’t have a solid ballhandler who can run the offense, and the result was Wake’s worst half of basketball this season. The Deacs consistently initiated the offense 25 feet from the basket and could never get any penetration inside the 3-point line, so they spent a large portion of the half passing the ball around the perimeter and either turning the ball over or forcing up a bad shot before the shot clock went off. Wake finished the first half with just 26 points, shooting 8-19 from the floor (42%) and turning the ball over 12 times. The Tigers ended the half on a 17-4 run to take an 11 point lead at the break. Things continued that way until about the 8 minute mark in the 2nd half, after the Tigers went up by 20 points. Trailing 49-69, a switch was seemingly flipped in the Deacs, and they suddenly woke up and started playing basketball again. Behind 27 2nd half points from Kennedy, Wake outscored the Tigers 36 to 19 over the final 8 minutes of the game, and clawed back to as close a 1 point with 9 seconds remaining. Kennedy was suddenly getting to the rim at will, and the Deacs were able to force 9 Memphis turnovers by picking up full court and trapping the ball. 27(!) in the second half for Kev! https://t.co/x8jmiE3o6V pic.twitter.com/OY03aAqvRd — Wake Forest Men's Basketball (@WakeMBB) November 27, 2026 Ultimately, the comeback fell short as Kennedy tripped on the final possession of the game, but credit Wake Forest for not giving up. After playing 32 terrible minutes of basketball and getting behind by 20 points, it would have been easy to just concede and go hang out in the resort, but the team continued to fight until the very end. Wake ends the Battle 4 Atlantis 1-1 with a win over Mississippi State and a narrow loss to a ranked Memphis Tigers team. The Deacs definitely still have a lot to improve on if they want to play in the postseason, but I think this team is probably a lot better than many of us were expecting them to be this season. LSU is up next. Go Deacs!

top.title: Lions get good news despite brutal loss to Bears
top.description: Lions get good news despite brutal loss to Bears originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Lions didn't have much to celebrate on Thanksgiving after their brutal loss to the Bears . The team lost at home, which is always a stinger. But what made it worse is that the team was winning for most of the game. The game turned into a heated Thanksgiving Day matchup that ended with a 39-35 win for the Bears. In the final few moments, Rome Odunze and Caleb Williams connected for a game-winning touchdown that Lions fans would like to forget. But all is not lost. There's still a reason for Lions fans to be optimistic after their heart-wrenching loss. Lions still have reason to be optimistic despite heartbreaking Thanksgiving loss Dan Parr of the NFL's official website believes the Lions still have hope. "The Lions' dreams aren't dead, even after a gutting loss," he says in a postgame piece. The biggest reason the Lions should be happy is because their playoff probability is still an impressive 87% after the game loss to the Bears, according to Next Gen Stats. A lot of teams would love that. However, their chance of winning the division is now 28%. "Dan Campbell's crew will need to regroup now, but it's capable of doing so with one of the league's elite offenses. The Lions are looking up at the Bears in the division now, but they have won six of their last seven, and their next two games are against the Falcons and Titans , who have a combined record of 4-16," he says. So all is not lost, and the Lions' offense is certainly elite. But they're going to have to really close out games and not let another Thanksgiving Day nightmare happen. top.title: Detroit Tigers’ Puzzling Beau Brieske Roster Move Suddenly Makes Sense
top.description: When the Detroit Tigers designated right-handed pitcher Beau Brieske for assignment on Friday afternoon, the move raised an interesting question. Why would the Tigers tender Brieske a contract for the 2027 season only to remove him from their 40-man roster a few days later? As it turns out, there may be a strategic reason behind the seemingly contradictory decisions. According to MLive Tigers beat reporter Evan Woodbery, the move could actually increase Detroit’s chances of keeping Brieske in the organization. Sep 22, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Tigers pitcher Beau Brieske (4) throws a pitch against the Washington Nationals in the ninth inning at Comerica Park. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Why the Detroit Tigers Designated Beau Brieske for Assignment The Tigers officially announced one-year contracts with Luis Gil and Ha-Seong Kim on Friday, designating Brieske and infielder Tsung-Che Cheng for assignment to accommodate the additions. However, Woodbery pointed out that Detroit previously used a similar strategy with outfielder Akil Baddoo. “Why DFA Brieske a few days after tendering him a contract for 2027?” Woodbery wrote on X . “Similar to what they did with Akil Baddoo a couple years ago: The tender could dissuade teams from claiming Brieske off waivers. If he goes unclaimed, he’ll be outrighted and become a well-paid Mud Hen.” Essentially, another team considering claiming Brieske off waivers would have to weigh the financial commitment associated with his tendered contract. That could make him a less attractive waiver claim, potentially allowing the Tigers to retain him in the minor leagues while freeing up a valuable 40-man roster spot. Could Beau Brieske Remain With the Tigers? Being designated for assignment does not necessarily mean Brieske’s time with the Tigers organization is over. If he clears outright waivers , Detroit could assign him to Triple-A Toledo, subject to his contractual and service-time rights. Of course, another organization could still claim Brieske, meaning there is some risk involved in the move. However, if Woodbery’s interpretation is correct, Scott Harris could ultimately free up a roster spot without losing a valuable pitching depth option. What initially appeared to be a head-scratching roster decision makes considerably more sense when viewed from that perspective.

top.title: Canucks Lose 3 Centers in Short Order: The Path Forward
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Vancouver Canucks centers are getting plucked and struck down one by one. Max Sasson has been traded , and then Elias Pettersson and Filip Chytil got hurt in the span of a week. Chytil was hurt in the latest game on Friday against the Philadelphia Flyers . Talk about bad timing for the team, as their depth will be greatly tested. Canucks Centers and Who Is Left? As it stands right now, Marco Rossi would be the undisputed number one center. Given his ice time and how Manny Malhotra has deployed him, it is not a good sign. However, it will be the best chance he will get to show his worth. Ty Mueller and Jacob Quillan have already been called up from Abbotsford and have played in the last four games for the NHL club. Paul Cotter and Drew O’Connor have played center this season for the Canucks, to mixed results. The Canucks will need to place either Elias Pettersson or Filip Chytil on injured reserve so they can call up an extra forward from Abbotsford. The Canucks could call up centers Riley Patterson, Akil Thomas , or Chase Wouters from the AHL. Patterson has the most points out of those three this season, with 11 points in 20 games for Abbotsford. Braeden Cootes has a reported hip injury, and the upcoming World Juniors championship is a priority. Therefore, he will likely not be the player called up in this situation. Centers to Keep an Eye On Marco Rossi stands out as the player to watch. If Chytil is out for an extended period of time, Rossi will be the first-line center. The question is, will Malhotra put him on the penalty kill? Chytil has played some PK minutes while Pettersson has been out. With just nine points in 28 games, there is no time like the present for Rossi to shine. If he does not, then questions will need to be answered. Ty Mueller is another center to watch. He has won 39 of 65 faceoffs (60%) in four games this season. His line alongside Drew O’Connor and Linus Karlsson has worked hard on the forecheck. He may be forced into a second-line role as the Canucks look thin up the middle. For Mueller, this may be the chance of a lifetime, and if he wants to carve out a role in the NHL, this is his time. top.title: Dolphins Target 31.5-Sack Edge Rusher For 2027 Draft
top.description: Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images John Blair, writing for NFL Mocks, projects the 2027 NFL Draft’s third overall selection by the Miami Dolphins to be Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons, according to a report . This choice aims to fix a gaping hole on the defensive line that has cost the team games all season. Blair believes Simmons brings the specific burst and motor Miami needs right now. The Dolphins currently sit at a 1-9 record, tied for the worst mark in the league behind only the Titans and Chargers. That standing puts them in line for the third pick if the draft were held today. The team needs a difference-maker on defense, and Simmons fits that bill perfectly according to the projection. Blair noted that Simmons has the tools to become a dominant pass rusher who disrupts opposing offenses. Why Simmons Fits the Need Simmons has put up massive numbers at Texas this season and over his career. In just eight games this year, he recorded 10.5 sacks and 16 tackles for loss. His career totals across 37 games include 123 tackles and a staggering 31.5 sacks. These stats show he can get to the quarterback consistently, something the current Dolphins roster struggles to do. Current starters Chop Robinson and Josh Uche have shown flashes but lack the long-term consistency Miami requires. Robinson was a speed pick in 2024, yet his strength remains a weakness that opponents exploit. Uche is only on a one-year deal and has just three sacks this season. The team simply cannot rely on these two players to carry the pass rush for years to come. The Cost of a Thin Roster The need for a new edge rusher becomes even more urgent when looking at the injuries plaguing the defensive line. Three defensive tackles suffered season-ending injuries for the Dolphins prior to their latest matchup versus the Bills. With Zach Sieler, Jordan Phillips, and Zeek Biggers gone, the team is short on bodies and depth. Coach Jeff Hafley has called the recent defensive performance a “big team effort” because everyone had to step up. Defensive coordinator Sean Duggan praised the physical and mental shape of the players who played heavy snaps. Despite the praise, the roster is thin, and the coaching staff knows they need more help to survive the rest of the season. The Dolphins will face the New York Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29, at Hard Rock Stadium with a 1-9 record and a 3-8 opponent.

top.title: Alonso on Chelsea fans’ Fofana chants and defeat to Nottingham Forest

nigeria.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Chairman of Agatu Local Government Area of Benue State, Mr Melvin Ejeh, has vowed to ensure the arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the killing of an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Inspector Anyebe Anya. Anya was reportedly killed by armed men who attacked him at his duty post at a checkpoint in Agatu a few days ago. The assailants were also said to have carted away his service rifle after the attack. Ejeh gave the assurance when he visited the deceased officer’s family in Otukpo to commiserate with them, describing Anya as a hardworking, honest and dedicated officer. He vowed that those behind the killing would not escape justice, assuring the bereaved family that efforts were already underway to track down and apprehend the perpetrators. “Those that killed him will not go unpunished. We will get all of them. I knew him personally. He was a very hardworking, honest man who was committed to his work. “The whole community is mourning his death. The people of Agatu are shocked and grieving over his death. “We console his family. He was a committed officer. I can assure you that we will get those involved and they will be brought to justice. There is a hunt for them already. “The entire Agatu people will not rest until he gets justice, that I can assure his family,” the chairman said. nigeria.title: Meet Emmanuel Emegha, Chelsea’s new striking sensation who has Nigerian roots

However, Emegha has chosen to represent the Netherlands internationally. He made his senior debut against Poland in November 2025, explaining that the Netherlands is his country and that he is proud to be Dutch. Although Nigeria missed out on having him represent the Super Eagles, his progress at Chelsea gives Nigerian fans another reason to follow his career closely. At 23, Emegha has the physical presence, pace and goalscoring instincts to make an impression in English football. nigeria.title: Chelsea beaten at Nottingham Forest as poor run continues
nigeria.description: Nottingham Forest claimed a memorable 3-2 victory over Chelsea at the City Ground on Friday night, November 27, piling further pressure on Blues manager Xabi Alonso after another disappointing performance from his side. Forest made a flying start to the encounter, taking the lead just five minutes into the game through Igor Jesus, who produced a superb volley from Daniel Muñoz’s cross to put the hosts ahead. Chelsea struggled to find their rhythm in the opening half, with Forest looking more dangerous and organised in attack. Despite enjoying more possession, the visitors failed to turn their dominance on the ball into meaningful goalscoring opportunities. The hosts doubled their advantage shortly after the restart when Morgan Gibbs-White converted from the penalty spot in the 51st minute. The penalty was awarded after Wesley Fofana brought down Liam Delap inside the Chelsea box. However, Chelsea responded three minutes later through substitute Emmanuel Emegha, who pulled one back after Pedro Neto’s effort took a deflection and fell kindly into his path. The goal briefly offered Chelsea hope of mounting a comeback, but Forest remained dangerous and restored their two-goal cushion in the 72nd minute when Gibbs-White grabbed his second of the evening. Chelsea refused to surrender, with Emegha scoring again in the 89th minute to reduce the deficit to 3-2 and set up a tense finish. However, Forest held on through the closing moments to secure all three points and condemn Chelsea to another painful defeat. nigeria.title: A Weekend For Proof
nigeria.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. That development changes the context of the coming days. Electoral preparation now requires visible progress on protection, accountability and public confidence alongside equipment and political agreements. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? How long did uploads take? How were exceptions resolved? A rehearsal can reveal problems that announcements cannot. Finding a fault early allows INEC to correct it. nigeria.title: Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand
nigeria.description: Two Nigerian men have been arrested in Thailand over their alleged links to an international romance scam network targeting victims across Southeast Asia. The suspects, aged 41 and 30, were arrested on November 18 at a condominium in Ban Mai, Pak Kret district, Nonthaburi, following an investigation by Thailand’s Immigration Division 3 and Provincial Police Region 1. According to local media outlet, The Thaiger, undercover police officers disguised themselves as food delivery workers to gain access to the suspects’ apartment. With the help of security guards, the officers approached the condominium and pretended to have a parcel for delivery. When one of the men opened the door, they identified themselves as police officers and moved in to arrest both suspects. A search of the apartment reportedly led to the recovery of laptops and mobile phones containing messages linked to fake online identities posing as US military personnel. Investigators suspect the identities were used to establish romantic relationships with potential victims as part of an international scam operation. Police also reportedly found social media accounts allegedly created to deceive Thai residents. The arrests followed an earlier investigation on November 12, when police detained another Nigerian man, aged 37, at Owl Market in Nonthaburi over suspected links to the same network. Investigators later searched a condominium in Bang Kraso, Mueang Nonthaburi, where suspected members of the group had reportedly stayed. However, the men had left before the search. Police subsequently traced the two suspects to another condominium in the Muang Thong Thani area, where they were believed to have stayed for two to three days before their arrest. The Thaiger reported that both men confessed during questioning. However, the charges publicly reported against them are immigration-related offences, including illegal entry and unauthorised residence. One of the suspects, aged 41, had reportedly overstayed his permitted stay in Thailand by 411 days. Authorities revoked their permission to remain in the country and transferred them to Pak Kret Police Station for further legal proceedings ahead of deportation. The investigation into the suspected romance scam network is ongoing. Thai police have not disclosed the identities of the alleged victims, the amount of money involved or the specific roles the two men allegedly played in the operation. nigeria.title: UK lists two conditions for bringing goods into country without paying tax
nigeria.description: The United Kingdom government has outlined two conditions under which travellers can bring goods into the country without paying customs duty or tax, warning that items outside the permitted categories or allowance limits could attract charges. According to the UK government’s customs guidelines, travellers can bring goods into the country tax-free under two conditions. First condition is personal use. Goods must be intended for the traveller’s own use rather than for commercial purposes or resale. Second condition is gifts. Travellers can also bring goods intended as presents for other people without paying customs duty, provided they remain within the applicable personal allowance. The rules apply to foreign visitors and British residents returning from overseas, regardless of whether the items were purchased from regular shops or duty-free outlets at airports. However, the exemptions are subject to personal allowance limits, which determine the quantity and value of goods travellers can bring into the country without incurring additional charges. The applicable allowance depends on where a traveller is arriving from and whether the destination is Great Britain, comprising England, Scotland and Wales, or Northern Ireland. The government also warned that goods intended for business or resale do not qualify for personal allowances. Such items must be declared to customs regardless of their value or quantity. Travellers are also required to declare goods that exceed their personal allowances or fall under banned and restricted categories before crossing the border. Declarations can be made online up to five days, or 120 hours, before arrival in the UK. The authorities warned that failure to comply with customs regulations could result in the seizure of goods and, in some cases, the vehicle used to transport them. Offenders may also face financial penalties or prosecution. The post UK lists two conditions for bringing goods into country without paying tax appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda
nigeria.description: Trials of an experimental Ebola vaccine launched in Uganda on Friday, while a global NGO said it had bought 1.5 million doses of another candidate, as the race heats up to contain the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo strain of Ebola behind the outbreak in DRC, which has caused more than 5,700 confirmed deaths out of more than 11,000 cases since being declared in May, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Two experimental vaccines are due to start testing on Monday in the outbreak’s epicentre in eastern DRC, the WHO said, focusing on contacts of cases and people deemed at high risk of infection. But neighbouring Uganda announced it had also launched a trial of one of the vaccines, developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid pandemic. The Uganda Virus Research Institute described it as “Africa’s first mRNA Phase I clinical trial”, conducted in collaboration with Moderna. It will test 224 healthy volunteers aged between one and 65 to measure its safety and immunity potential. The other potential vaccine is the ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector vaccine developed by India’s Serum Institute and the University of Oxford — which will also begin testing in DRC on Monday. But Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, which brings together government and private donors to help developing countries acquire jabs at affordable prices, is not waiting around. After the Covid-19 pandemic, the alliance set up a new $50 million First Response Fund — under a so-called “No Regrets” approach — to allow it to buy up doses in advance even before they have been fully tested. – Deployment – Gavi signed a purchase commitment this week with the Serum Institute for 1.5 million doses of the ChAdOx1, and plans to have “hundreds of thousands” ready to deploy should the trials prove successful and they are approved by the WHO and DRC government. “We’re investing in it, hoping that the signals will be positive, and if that is the case, we’ll have gained months and months on the deployment,” Emanuele Capobianco, Gavi’s director of global health security, told AFP. He said he hoped for trials to conclude “within the first half of 2027” and even “within the first quarter” in a more optimistic scenario. Gavi also has a stockpile of 500,000 doses of an existing vaccine, Ervebo, used against the Zaire strain of Ebola, which began testing last month to see if it is also effective against Bundibugyo. Despite a long and porous border with eastern DRC, Uganda has successfully contained the virus after receiving some imported cases earlier this year. It was declared Ebola-free in August after registering 20 cases, including two deaths. The post mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Nigeria set to bid to host maiden U-17 WAFCON
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigeria is preparing to bid to host the maiden edition of the Under-17 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), as the country seeks to attract more international sporting competitions and strengthen its sports economy. The Director-General of the National Sports Commission (NSC), Bukola Olopade, disclosed this in a video shared on his X handle on Friday, saying Nigeria had already communicated its interest to the Confederation of African Football (CAF). Three people familiar with the matter told Reuters that the intrusion was discovered within the past month during efforts to upgrade the system, triggering disruptions across the platform. It said: “We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities.” A major military computing platform Launched in 2017, Cloud One was designed as a centralised platform for the Air Force’s information technology needs, bringing together services provided by four major technology companies: Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet. The platform supports dozens of applications, including systems managing personnel records, salaries, logistics and military equipment maintenance. nigeria.title: France slips into ‘technical recession’ after GDP revision
nigeria.description: France’s economy has slipped into a technical recession after revised official figures showed that gross domestic product (GDP) contracted in the third quarter, extending the country’s economic decline. The National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE) said on Friday that the eurozone’s second-largest economy shrank by 0.2 per cent in the third quarter, revising its initial estimate of a 0.1 per cent contraction. The agency also revised second-quarter growth downwards to 0.02 per cent from zero per cent previously, although the figure was rounded to zero in the headline data. The revisions mean France’s economy has recorded consecutive quarterly contractions since the end of last year, meeting the conventional definition of a technical recession, which is two successive quarters of negative economic growth. The latest figures pose additional challenges for the government as it struggles to rein in the country’s budget deficit, with its target of 0.5 per cent economic growth this year now appearing increasingly difficult to achieve. The minority government is also facing difficulties securing parliamentary approval for its 2027 budget, which seeks to reduce the fiscal deficit from 5.4 per cent of GDP this year to five per cent next year. The budget debate comes five months before France’s presidential election, amid deep divisions in parliament. Reacting to the figures, Finance Minister Roland Lescure called for the speedy adoption of the budget, insisting that the five per cent deficit target was non-negotiable. “We must adopt a budget as soon as possible with a non-negotiable deficit target of 5%. It is imperative that we restore visibility for economic stakeholders,” he said. A breakdown of the third-quarter GDP figures by INSEE showed that weak domestic demand contributed to the contraction. Consumer spending rose by 0.3 per cent, but this was offset by a 0.8 per cent decline in business investment. The rebuilding of business inventories contributed 0.3 percentage points to GDP growth, following a 0.7 percentage-point reduction in the previous quarter. Foreign trade also weighed heavily on economic performance, subtracting 0.6 percentage points from output as exports fell by 1.6 per cent while imports increased by 0.1 per cent. Despite the contraction, the Bank of France said earlier in November that the economy was expected to record moderate growth in the fourth quarter. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June Galaxy has withdrawn its October call that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June, saying the technical signal behind it failed after seven straight weeks of losses and that the bear market is “very likely not over.” Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, laid out the reversal in a report published Wednesday and sent to clients a day earlier. “We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June,” the report said. “The signal it rested on has failed.” The firm’s Oct. 26 note had argued that bitcoin had entered an accumulation phase. Galaxy said at the time that a weekly close back below the 50-week moving average that was not regained within a month would invalidate its technical case. That is what happened. Bitcoin closed the week ended Nov. 8 at $74,968, 0.7% below the 50-week average, after seven weekly closes above it. It then closed the week ended Nov. 15 below the 200-week average, which Galaxy has described as the floor of past bear markets. Galaxy points to $58,525 The week ended Nov. 22 closed at $61,104, 17.9% below the 50-week average and 10.4% below the 200-week average of $68,159. Bitcoin traded below its July 1 intraday low on Nov. 20 and reached $55,100 on Nov. 21, but the June 30 closing low of $58,525 held on a daily basis through Nov. 22. Galaxy now treats that level as the line to watch. A daily close below $58,525 would be “the start of a move to a materially lower low,” the report said, and the firm would not treat such a close as a buying signal by itself. History is not kind to breaks like that. In the seven prior bear market cases where bitcoin closed below a low that had stood for at least 60 days, the eventual low was at least 17% lower, with a median of 52%. Applied to the June low, that works out to about $48,500 and $28,200. Bitcoin briefly slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday morning as the Nasdaq sank, but it ended the day back above $60,000 and has not posted a daily close below $58,525. It traded near $60,800 on Thursday morning. Late by the clock, early by the depth Galaxy said two readings of the market disagree. By the calendar, this bear is old: Nov. 22 was day 412 since the Oct. 6, 2025, record, longer than the 163 to 406 days from high to low in the four prior bear markets. By depth, it looks unfinished. Bitcoin’s 53% decline compares with drops of 77% to 93% in earlier bears. It also has not closed a day below its realized price of $53,205, something every prior bear did for at least 140 days, and only two of the 13 bottom signals Galaxy tracks have been met. “The clock says this bear is overdue to end, the depth says it has further to fall, and we do not believe the price record alone can settle which,” the report said. Flows have not helped. Galaxy estimates U.S. spot bitcoin ETPs hold about 1.24 million BTC, 9.7% below their October 2025 peak, after shedding 71,339 BTC, or $4.95 billion, since Oct. 4. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. entertainment.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: Recap: Wake Forest’s Comeback Effort Falls Short in 85-88 Loss to #24 Memphis
sports.description: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 05: Kevair Kennedy #55 of the Wake Forest Demon Deacons looks on during the second half of the game against the Vanderbilt Commodores at Memorial Gym on November 05, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the final game of the Battle 4 Atlantis, the Deacs dropped their 2nd game of the season to the Memphis Tigers by a score of 85-88. Unbelievable fight falls just short. pic.twitter.com/MAGB94YP9e — Wake Forest Men's Basketball (@WakeMBB) November 27, 2026 The game started off fine for the Deacs, but after Kevair Kennedy picked up his 2nd foul just 6 minutes into the game, things fell apart rapidly. When Kennedy exited the game, the Deacs held a 13-8 lead with 14 minutes remaining in the half—Wake scored 13 points total in those final 14 minutes. Without Kennedy, the Deacs just don’t have a solid ballhandler who can run the offense, and the result was Wake’s worst half of basketball this season. The Deacs consistently initiated the offense 25 feet from the basket and could never get any penetration inside the 3-point line, so they spent a large portion of the half passing the ball around the perimeter and either turning the ball over or forcing up a bad shot before the shot clock went off. Wake finished the first half with just 26 points, shooting 8-19 from the floor (42%) and turning the ball over 12 times. The Tigers ended the half on a 17-4 run to take an 11 point lead at the break. Things continued that way until about the 8 minute mark in the 2nd half, after the Tigers went up by 20 points. Trailing 49-69, a switch was seemingly flipped in the Deacs, and they suddenly woke up and started playing basketball again. Behind 27 2nd half points from Kennedy, Wake outscored the Tigers 36 to 19 over the final 8 minutes of the game, and clawed back to as close a 1 point with 9 seconds remaining. Kennedy was suddenly getting to the rim at will, and the Deacs were able to force 9 Memphis turnovers by picking up full court and trapping the ball. 27(!) in the second half for Kev! https://t.co/x8jmiE3o6V pic.twitter.com/OY03aAqvRd — Wake Forest Men's Basketball (@WakeMBB) November 27, 2026 Ultimately, the comeback fell short as Kennedy tripped on the final possession of the game, but credit Wake Forest for not giving up. After playing 32 terrible minutes of basketball and getting behind by 20 points, it would have been easy to just concede and go hang out in the resort, but the team continued to fight until the very end. Wake ends the Battle 4 Atlantis 1-1 with a win over Mississippi State and a narrow loss to a ranked Memphis Tigers team. The Deacs definitely still have a lot to improve on if they want to play in the postseason, but I think this team is probably a lot better than many of us were expecting them to be this season. sports.title: Detroit Tigers’ Puzzling Beau Brieske Roster Move Suddenly Makes Sense
sports.description: When the Detroit Tigers designated right-handed pitcher Beau Brieske for assignment on Friday afternoon, the move raised an interesting question. Why would the Tigers tender Brieske a contract for the 2027 season only to remove him from their 40-man roster a few days later? As it turns out, there may be a strategic reason behind the seemingly contradictory decisions. According to MLive Tigers beat reporter Evan Woodbery, the move could actually increase Detroit’s chances of keeping Brieske in the organization. Sep 22, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Tigers pitcher Beau Brieske (4) throws a pitch against the Washington Nationals in the ninth inning at Comerica Park. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Why the Detroit Tigers Designated Beau Brieske for Assignment The Tigers officially announced one-year contracts with Luis Gil and Ha-Seong Kim on Friday, designating Brieske and infielder Tsung-Che Cheng for assignment to accommodate the additions. However, Woodbery pointed out that Detroit previously used a similar strategy with outfielder Akil Baddoo. “Why DFA Brieske a few days after tendering him a contract for 2027?” Woodbery wrote on X . “Similar to what they did with Akil Baddoo a couple years ago: The tender could dissuade teams from claiming Brieske off waivers. If he goes unclaimed, he’ll be outrighted and become a well-paid Mud Hen.” Essentially, another team considering claiming Brieske off waivers would have to weigh the financial commitment associated with his tendered contract. That could make him a less attractive waiver claim, potentially allowing the Tigers to retain him in the minor leagues while freeing up a valuable 40-man roster spot. Could Beau Brieske Remain With the Tigers? Being designated for assignment does not necessarily mean Brieske’s time with the Tigers organization is over. If he clears outright waivers , Detroit could assign him to Triple-A Toledo, subject to his contractual and service-time rights. Of course, another organization could still claim Brieske, meaning there is some risk involved in the move. However, if Woodbery’s interpretation is correct, Scott Harris could ultimately free up a roster spot without losing a valuable pitching depth option. What initially appeared to be a head-scratching roster decision makes considerably more sense when viewed from that perspective.

Talk about bad timing for the team, as their depth will be greatly tested. Canucks Centers and Who Is Left? As it stands right now, Marco Rossi would be the undisputed number one center. Braeden Cootes has a reported hip injury, and the upcoming World Juniors championship is a priority. Therefore, he will likely not be the player called up in this situation. Centers to Keep an Eye On Marco Rossi stands out as the player to watch. If Chytil is out for an extended period of time, Rossi will be the first-line center. sports.title: Dolphins Target 31.5-Sack Edge Rusher For 2027 Draft
sports.description: Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images John Blair, writing for NFL Mocks, projects the 2027 NFL Draft’s third overall selection by the Miami Dolphins to be Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons, according to a report . This choice aims to fix a gaping hole on the defensive line that has cost the team games all season. Blair believes Simmons brings the specific burst and motor Miami needs right now. The Dolphins currently sit at a 1-9 record, tied for the worst mark in the league behind only the Titans and Chargers. That standing puts them in line for the third pick if the draft were held today. The team needs a difference-maker on defense, and Simmons fits that bill perfectly according to the projection. Blair noted that Simmons has the tools to become a dominant pass rusher who disrupts opposing offenses. Why Simmons Fits the Need Simmons has put up massive numbers at Texas this season and over his career. In just eight games this year, he recorded 10.5 sacks and 16 tackles for loss. His career totals across 37 games include 123 tackles and a staggering 31.5 sacks. These stats show he can get to the quarterback consistently, something the current Dolphins roster struggles to do. Current starters Chop Robinson and Josh Uche have shown flashes but lack the long-term consistency Miami requires. Robinson was a speed pick in 2024, yet his strength remains a weakness that opponents exploit. Uche is only on a one-year deal and has just three sacks this season. The team simply cannot rely on these two players to carry the pass rush for years to come. The Cost of a Thin Roster The need for a new edge rusher becomes even more urgent when looking at the injuries plaguing the defensive line. Three defensive tackles suffered season-ending injuries for the Dolphins prior to their latest matchup versus the Bills. With Zach Sieler, Jordan Phillips, and Zeek Biggers gone, the team is short on bodies and depth. Coach Jeff Hafley has called the recent defensive performance a “big team effort” because everyone had to step up. Defensive coordinator Sean Duggan praised the physical and mental shape of the players who played heavy snaps. Despite the praise, the roster is thin, and the coaching staff knows they need more help to survive the rest of the season. The Dolphins will face the New York Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29, at Hard Rock Stadium with a 1-9 record and a 3-8 opponent.

sports.title: FSU beats South Carolina in PKs to advance to third round of NCAA Tournament
sports.description: No. 5 seed Florida State women’s soccer defeated No. 4 seed South Carolina in penalty kicks (PKs) in the second round of the NCAA Tournament on Friday at Vanderbilt in Nashville, keeping their national championship defense alive. After a full 90 minutes and two 10-minute overtime periods, the teams remained tied at 1-1, forcing a penalty shootout that the Seminoles won 7-6. Competing in temperatures around 45 degrees, seven Seminoles played the full 90 minutes of regulation: Wrianna Hudson, Kate Ockene, Bridget Mutipula, Janet Okeke, Grace Hoytink, Nawreen Ahmad and Peyton McGovern. Six of those players remained on the field through both overtime periods, with Ockene exiting due to an injury early in the first overtime. South Carolina struck first in the 29th minute when Cuyler Zulauf found the back of the net, giving the Gamecocks a 1-0 advantage. Despite trailing at halftime, Florida State outshot South Carolina 6-2. However, both of the Gamecocks’ shots were on goal, while the Seminoles had yet to record a shot on goal. Florida State came out with renewed energy in the second half, finding the equalizer in the 55th minute when Okeke scored off a corner kick from Joelle Jung. The Seminoles continued to build momentum and apply offensive pressure, recording three corner kicks in the second half after having none in the first. Florida State nearly took the lead following a strong passing sequence that ended with Jung sending a shot over the crossbar. At the end of 90 minutes, the Seminoles had outshot the Gamecocks 17-7, with both teams recording three shots on goal. In the second minute of the first overtime period, Ockene went down with an injury. She was replaced by junior goalkeeper Fernanda Mayrink, who had made one start for Florida State this season. Mayrink made an immediate impact, stopping the ball following a South Carolina corner kick. She remained in goal for the remainder of overtime, recording a save. Florida State finished with 22 shots, including three on goal, but neither team was able to find the game-winning goal in either overtime period, sending the match to PKs. Nyanya Touray took Florida State’s first PK, but her attempt bounced off the post. South Carolina’s Ava Tutas converted her attempt to give the Gamecocks an early advantage. Hudson converted Florida State’s second attempt, followed by a successful PK from Zulauf to maintain South Carolina’s lead. Ahmad scored for the Seminoles before Reagan Schubach missed her attempt for the Gamecocks, evening the score at 2-2. Mayrink stepped up and converted her PK to give Florida State a 3-2 advantage, but Reese Slater responded for South Carolina. Lara Dantas converted for the Seminoles before Maggie Taitano answered for the Gamecocks, sending the shootout into sudden death with the teams tied at 4-4. technology.title: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
technology.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. technology.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
technology.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. technology.title: UK government rejects national consultation on AI datacenters
technology.description: The UK government has rejected calls for a UK-wide public consultation on the environmental impacts of AI datacenters, despite a petition attracting more than 39,000 signatures. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. They also provide the infrastructure needed to develop and use AI," the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) says. "Building more capacity in the UK will support economic growth and innovation, while strengthening national resilience and ensuring the UK is well placed to realize the opportunities presented by AI." But it adds that the government recognizes the environmental impacts of bit barns are real and must be understood and mitigated, and this is one of the reasons why it established the Data Centre Covenant tests. This Covenant, published last month, sets out tests all compute sheds "are encouraged to meet," while "strategic datacenters" are required to meet them to qualify for additional government assistance. The government has yet to define which datacenters qualify as "strategic," saying it will publish further details and eligibility criteria in due course. Qualifying projects could receive help securing power and accelerating planning. Briefly, the Covenant tests are that operators cover any energy costs they create, so that communities do not have to pick up the bill; that they invest in local communities; adhere to the highest environmental standards; create jobs and drive reindustrialization; and provide secure and reliable access to their compute resources. If this has a ring of familiarity, it is because President Trump earlier this year introduced a Ratepayer Protection Pledge , under which hyperscalers and AI companies agreed to protect US consumers from any bill shocks due to the energy and infrastructure requirements of their datacenter projects. It seems that where the US leads, the UK still often follows. technology.title: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
technology.description: Europe's IT spending is growing more slowly than the global average, according to Gartner, whose analysts warn that the region's push for tech sovereignty faces commercial and technological obstacles. Gartner forecasts European IT spending of $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9 percent from 2026, compared with worldwide growth of 15 percent to $7.35 trillion. For 2026, it estimates spending growth of 20.7 percent in North America and 13.7 percent in China. "The world seems to be racing towards this AI goal of where the large language model provider is going to be, and the race seems to be between North American-based providers and some Asia Pacific providers," John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, told The Register . He said Europe had traditionally trailed in IT uptake. "We saw that happen when global sourcing, cloud, and software as a service all came along. It's down to the pushback against the idea of creative destruction," where new technologies replace old ones. Europe's fastest growing categories are datacenter systems, forecast to grow 29.7 percent in 2027, and infrastructure as a service, at 26.7 percent. Even so, Lovelock does not expect Europe to compete with North America and China on AI investment. "For AI provision, Europe is going to be behind, and there won't be a way to catch up," he said. "The AI datacenters, the large language models, the foundational models, the tools and techniques for building out AI are all being centered outside of Europe, but enterprises don't need to do that. So the question becomes: regardless of where the source of the AI is coming from, can the enterprises actually adopt and use it? In one sense, Europe will be behind in the provision of AI, but it need not be behind in the use." The gap nonetheless complicates Europe's push to reduce its dependence on US technology suppliers. The European Union has introduced new rules to encourage tech buyers to favor sovereign tech over the dominant tech vendors, but Lovelock doubts they will move spending much. "Sovereignty is a wonderful flag that we fly on the front of a building. IT is running in the basement. CIOs are not going to buy a second-best solution that costs more simply because it's sovereign. "They are not going to break any laws, but they are not going to make a decision that puts their company in a worse position at a higher cost. While sovereignty gets [vendors] on the list, it doesn't assure that they get purchased," he told us. Earlier this month, Gartner predicted that by 2029, more than 90 percent of EU organizations will have a digital sovereignty strategy, but argued that a fully sovereign technology stack remains out of reach. "The global technology supply chain is too interconnected, and many critical dependencies cannot be replaced at a commercially viable scale," said Bettina Tratz-Ryan, VP analyst at Gartner. ®

science.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
science.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.

science.title: Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still
science.description: null Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone. The five stars are still there, but the shape you may have memorized looks like it's been picked up and turned over. It looks more like an E or an M, depending on when you look. Now try and look for the Big Dipper /the Plough. It's gone. Nothing mysterious has happened, of course. Cassiopeia is doing exactly what it always does, but it's a reminder that the northern sky is where you can easily watch the stars move — and the seasons turn. What's happening and when to look Stars move anti-clockwise around the north celestial pole, so Cassiopeia changes orientation. (Image credit: Alan Dyer/Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) Late November is an excellent time to reacquaint yourself with Cassiopeia from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. Look high in the northern sky during the evening for its five prominent stars — Caph, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah and Segin. Depending on exactly when you look, it can look like a W, E, M or a 3. This is because Cassiopeia is circumpolar. Rather than rising in the east and eventually setting in the west like many familiar constellations , it circles the north celestial pole — a position currently held by Polaris , the North Star. From sufficiently northerly latitudes, its main stars never disappear below the horizon. This gives us a simple observing experiment. Find Cassiopeia in the early evening and remember its orientation relative to the horizon. Go back several hours later and look again. The constellation has moved around Polaris, and its shape has changed. The stars haven't changed their arrangement — Earth has simply rotated from west to east. We all know this logically, but watching the familiar pattern of Cassiopeia's stars apparently tip over during a single night makes Earth's rotation a lot less abstract.
